newsitem.title: USA: Texas wheat condition improves slightly.
newsitem.headline: Texas wheat condition improves slightly.

text.p: Texas wheat condition improved and farmers made good progress on fieldwork during the week ended Sunday, the state's agricultural statistics service said in its weekly crop progress report.
Statewide, wheat was rated 31 percent good to excellent, 37 fair and 32 poor to very poor. That compared to last week's ratings of 27 percent good to excellent, 41 fair, and 32 poor to very poor.
Despite the slight improvement, there was still visible damage from the April freeze. Isolated hail damage also caused damage in some fields, the report said.
Wheat was 66 percent headed versus 80 a year ago and the five-year average of 73.

Corn was 81 percent planted compared to 93 a year ago and the 92 average. Warmer temperatures in the Plains for most of the week helped emergence. Statewide the crop was rated at 77 percent of normal compared with 62 percent last year.
Sorghum planting advanced to 56 percent versus 63 a year ago and the 69 average. The crop was rated 75 percent good to excellent, 19 fair, and six poor to very poor.
Cotton planting slowly increased as soil temperatures warmed. Overall, 27 percent of the state's cotton acreage was planted, on par with last year but lagging the average of 32.
